title: Harbor and Bridge
premise: In 1747, Elodie Winterbourne keeps the harbor light at Greyhaven and an unofficial ledger of every soul who passes through—debtors, deserters, drowned sailors, and the found family that has gathered around her since her husband's death. When the Crown requisitions the town for war and orders all records seized, Elodie realizes the ledger is the only proof that certain people ever existed, including a smuggler's daughter the garrison means to erase. Over one brutal storm season she hides pages, copies names from memory, and races a victor's historian who arrives to write the official account. The book ends with Elodie surrendering a decoy ledger to the army while the true record travels to safety in the hands of the girl it was written to protect.
about_author: Orsen Lockridge is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse station logs along the northern coast. Harbor and Bridge is his third novel, drawn from a real requisition ledger he once found misfiled in a customs house basement.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She trims the lamp, logs a wrecked fishing crew, and adds three new names to her private ledger—the town's unofficial memory. Establishes her widowed solitude and the found family orbiting the light: Tam the mute boatboy, Mrs. Quill the midwife, and Joss Renner, a smuggler with a daughter named Wren. Beat: quiet devotion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The girl helps Elodie salvage cargo from a wreck and learns to read using the ledger itself. A navy cutter is sighted on the horizon, earlier than any season warrants. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by first unease.

chapters.title: Orders in a Sealed Hand
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A requisition notice arrives: the Crown claims Greyhaven as a supply port; all registers, rolls, and records must be surrendered within the month. The harbormaster urges compliance. Elodie lies awake counting what can be carried. Beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: The Historian
chapters.summary: Mr. Aldous Vane's POV. The Crown's historian arrives aboard the cutter, ambitious and precise, tasked with writing the official history of the occupation. He interviews Elodie about shipping traffic and notes her ledger with professional interest. Beat: a courteous predator enters the story.

chapters.title: Joss Renner's Debts
chapters.summary: Joss's POV. The smuggler confesses his name appears in seized customs papers under charges that could hang him, and that Wren's mother was never legally recorded at all. He asks Elodie what the ledger says about them. Beat: the stakes turn personal and mortal.

chapters.title: Copying by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She begins a hidden duplicate of the ledger, enlisting Mrs. Quill to verify names and dates from memory. Tam ferries pages to a cache in the sea cave. First storm of the season hits. Beat: conspiracy of tenderness.

chapters.title: The Garrison Takes the Town
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Soldiers billet in homes; the church becomes a storehouse; the school closes. Wren watches soldiers burn 'surplus' papers in the square and understands what surrendering the ledger would mean. Beat: innocence ending.

chapters.title: An Interview by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Vane questions Elodie again, probing discrepancies between her memory and the harbor register he now holds. He suspects nothing yet but admires her precision—a dangerous compliment. Beat: cat and mouse begins.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Low Water
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The mute boy carries copied pages across the tidal bridge to a sympathetic excise officer's widow inland. He is nearly caught by a patrol and hides the pages inside his coat against his heart. Beat: fear transformed into courage.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The great storm cracks the lantern room; Elodie keeps the light burning by hand through the night while the garrison demands laborers instead. Her refusal to abandon the lamp earns grudging respect—and scrutiny. Beat: endurance as defiance.

chapters.title: What Vane Found
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Comparing water-damaged originals with his own notes, Vane finds a name missing from the official register: Wren's mother. He confronts Elodie gently, offering protection in exchange for the full truth. Beat: temptation offered.

chapters.title: Mrs. Quill's Testimony
chapters.summary: Mrs. Quill's POV. The old midwife recounts forty years of births and deaths the parish never recorded, including Wren's mother's. She insists names outlive paperwork. Elodie decides the duplicate must be finished before the seizure date. Beat: inheritance of memory.

chapters.title: The Decoy
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. With Joss's help she fabricates a plausible but incomplete second ledger—accurate enough to pass inspection, silent on the people who matter. Guilt and resolve wrestle as she practices lying to Vane's face. Beat: moral cost accepted.

chapters.title: Surrender Day
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The garrison collects all records in the square. Elodie hands over the decoy with steady hands while Wren, watching, understands for the first time what her guardian has built. Vane accepts the ledger—but lingers. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Reviewing the surrendered ledger, Vane notices ink consistent with recent copying and a margin mark matching Elodie's habit. He says nothing to his superiors—yet—and requests one more interview. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: Joss Is Taken
chapters.summary: Joss's POV. Soldiers arrest Joss on the old smuggling charges, citing papers Vane's clerks have indexed. In the cell he refuses to give up Wren's whereabouts. Elodie realizes the historian holds his fate. Beat: despair's floor.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Victor
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She offers Vane a trade: her testimony and the true story of the town's erased people for Joss's release and Wren's safe passage. Vane, torn between career and conscience, asks for a night to decide. Beat: unlikely alliance forming.

chapters.title: The Night of the Second Storm
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The season's worst storm strikes during the exchange: the light fails, a transport founders, and Elodie, Vane, and Tam work the lamp together while Joss escapes in the chaos. Beat: crisis forging strange fellowship.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. By lamplight, Vane takes down sworn testimony—every name, birth, debt, and drowning—including Wren's mother, entering it into his own official history where no one can strike it out. Beat: triumph through the enemy's own instrument.

chapters.title: Departures
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vane arranges Joss's pardon and escorts Wren inland to the widow who will keep her, carrying the original ledger sewn into her coat. Goodbyes at the bridge; Tam gives her his carved gull. Beat: grief braided with hope.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Spring comes; the garrison withdraws. Elodie writes the final entry in her working ledger—her own name, at last, among the people she kept—and relights the lamp for the season's first clear night. Beat: self-recognition.

chapters.title: Harbor and Bridge
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Vane's POV, years later. His published history carries the names intact; a grown Wren visits Greyhaven with the original ledger, returning it to its keeper. The two records, official and private, sit side by side. Beat: memory inherited, family chosen, light still burning.
